# Explicit quantum fold boundary

Implemented under #194 and the adopted edition-2026 QS/PR/RS/EXACT obligations. `qfor static` carries quantum-containing values; `for static` carries ordinary values. Both use the original common source judgment and existing deterministic fold elaboration/native gates. No new primitive, capacity, acceptance authority or proof discharge is introduced.

The informed [first context](context.md), [session](session.json) and original attempt-01 are preserved. Actual checks expose source-author mistakes and unsupported closed dyadic-control lowering; later attempts are explicit repairs, never replacements for first attempts. The final bounded QPE client uses existing CNOT phase kickback. Closed GHZ/arithmetic/mixed-carry/ordinary distributions and zero-width amplitude are checked independently.

[Validation](implementation-validation.json) distinguishes tests, numerical conformance, pending authoring work, current identity checks and older hosted CI. [Surface review](implementation-surface-review.json) records the token/AST change and unchanged capacities/native boundary. [Active test migration](active-test-migration.json) binds the predecessor files; the small `tests/fixtures/frontend_v030/qfor/source-map.json` selects current derivatives without editing corpus originals or historical authoring sources. Fixed historical Fourier regression sources only migrate their fold spelling; generic QFT remains outside the goal.

No blind-model performance, full source-preservation theorem, broad constitutional certification or Issue completion is claimed.

## Reference-only first authoring, 2026-10-27

The separate [archive](reference-first.tar.xz), [pinned index](reference-first-index.json)
and [observation summary](reference-first-validation.json) retain two authors
configured with fresh contexts and only the frozen tasks/Reference extracts.
Each produced GHZ, mod-2 accumulation and one-bit phase-kickback programs.
All three current-spelling project sources work on their first submission.
All three historical-spelling sources also work after a token-only header
translation to the current grammar. Both cohorts needed zero author repairs;
this small comparison shows no repair-rate advantage.

All 48 actual CLI observations and six unchanged first sources are retained.
The twelve successful runs match the independent small-system distributions.
Direct current-CLI rejection of the retired spelling is separate from the
controlled spelling comparison. Private project mains are valid; the twelve
selected-private refusals reflect an observer precondition omitted from the
prompt. Separate public-exposure inputs supply that precondition and count as
observer setup, rather than author repairs. No original is overwritten.

This is a surface-spelling comparison using current semantics, rather than an
old-compiler replay or a population-level model benchmark. The configured
context isolation and participant tool-use reports are recorded; model build,
sampling seed and independent tool transcripts were not separately pinned.
The retained CLI identity is not fresh compilation attestation. The earlier
informed study, fixed-Fourier regressions and generic-QFT exclusion remain
unchanged. Required candidate CI/review and the final Issue audit are separate.

The maintained [current derivatives](../../frontend_v030/qfor/reference-current/)
have their own [edition manifest](../../frontend_v030/qfor/reference-current/Qargo.toml).
Four distinct current inputs cover both authors' preparations; identical
GHZ/accumulator bodies are shared. `tests/qfor.rs` freshly compiles these inputs
through the current selected Raw frontend, obtains native acceptance and checks
the independent distributions. These active regressions never execute the
historical archive or change its first sources and observations.
